exhibits.title: The Endless Stacks
exhibits.text: An ever-growing library where the books are never reshelved. The query is the question you walk in with, the key is the label on each spine, the value is the content within. At training time the whole library is read at once, all Q, K, V computed together, the full (n, n) score matrix in parallel, no cache needed. At inference the model writes one word at a time, and re-reading every past book each step would be madness. So it keeps a KV CACHE: as each token is produced, its key and value are shelved forever. The next word needs only the new query, scored against every shelved key. Watch above: spoken tokens cool to blue as their K/V are shelved; the gold query rides the newest word. The library only grows; it is never re-derived.

exhibits.title: Why the Asker Is Not Kept
exhibits.text: Generating 'The cat sat on': after prefilling 'The cat', the caches hold K=[k_The, k_cat], V=[v_The, v_cat]. To decode 'sat', compute only q_sat, k_sat, v_sat; shelve the new key and value; score q_sat against all three keys -> weights like [0.12, 0.55, 0.33]; blend -> one vector -> MLP -> vocabulary -> next word. Notice Q is NOT cached. We could keep a Q-cache and multiply it by the keys, but we would only ever use its last row, every earlier row recomputes an answer already spoken. The query is the ASKER: it asks once and moves on. The key and value are the LABEL and the CONTENT: they must remain for every future asker. This is no RNN hoping the past is squeezed into one state. Every new query has DIRECT access to every past key and value. Nothing is compressed away.

exhibits.title: The Two Rhythms, The Transformer Block
exhibits.text: A whole Transformer is this room repeated: talk, then think, L times. ATTENTION is inter-token, 'who should I listen to?', like the spatial mixing of a convolution, tokens looking at other tokens. The MLP is intra-token, 'what do I do with what I heard?', like a 1x1 conv, each token processed alone (d -> 4d -> GELU -> d). The pre-LayerNorm block: x -> LayerNorm -> Multi-Head Attention -> + residual -> LayerNorm -> MLP -> + residual. Residual connections are the information highway (as in ResNet): each layer learns only a delta, and gradients flow straight through. LayerNorm keeps activations sane. Input shape equals output shape, (n, d_model), which is why blocks stack cleanly, L = 32 for a 7B model, L = 96 for a GPT-4-class one.

exhibits.title: Flash in the Antechamber
exhibits.text: The cost is not only compute but MEMORY TRAFFIC. Eager attention writes the full (n, n) score matrix to the GPU's large-but-slow HBM: at n = 128K that is ~32 GB for ONE head of ONE layer. Flash Attention never forms that matrix. It works in TILES: load a block of Q and K into the tiny fast on-chip SRAM (~20 MB), compute partial scores, fold them into a running softmax (running max m, running sum l, old partials rescaled by e^(m_old − m_new)), accumulate the output, discard the block, like the tiles flickering above. Memory drops from O(n²) to O(n) and the result is IDENTICAL: a traced example gives [5.62, 3.30] eager or tiled. If Flash and eager ever disagree, it is a bug, not a feature.

exhibits.title: The Bookends, Embedding and lm_head
exhibits.text: Two learned layers bracket every Transformer. The token embedding turns a vocabulary index into a d_model vector: a table of shape (vocab_size, d_model), but only the n looked-up rows are touched per forward pass (a sparse gather). At the far end, the lm_head / W_vocab projects d_model back to vocab_size logits, always a full matrix multiply. Many models TIE them, setting W_vocab equal to the transpose of the embedding table. A quiet consequence: during training only the rows that were looked up receive gradient, so rare tokens get fewer updates and end up with poorer embeddings.

exhibits.title: The Decode Loop with KV Cache
exhibits.spec:
graph TD
  N[new token] --> Q[compute q, k, v for it]
  Q --> A[append k,v to KV cache]
  A --> SC[scores = q · K_cacheᵀ → 1×t]
  SC --> SM[softmax → weights]
  SM --> O[blend V_cache → one vector]
  O --> MLP[MLP]
  MLP --> LM[lm_head → next token]
  LM --> N
exhibits.caption: Q is fresh each step; K and V only ever grow. One loop, one token at a time.

exhibits.title: The KV cache at inference: the library only grows
exhibits.caption: Two readings of the same truth: the cache only grows. Left, the staircase, generating 'The cat sat on the mat', the number of cached (K, V) vectors rises by exactly one per decode step. The prompt 'The cat' is read in one PREFILL pass (two vectors shelved at once); thereafter each DECODE step shelves one more. Right, the rhythm of a single decode step producing 'sat': the new token's q, k, v are computed FRESH; k_sat and v_sat are appended to the caches (shelved forever); q_sat is scored against every cached key (q . K_cache^T), softmaxed to weights like [.12 .55 .33], then used to blend the cached values into one vector that flows through the MLP and lm_head to the next token. Note what is NOT kept: Q. The query is the asker, it asks once and moves on, so caching it would only ever reuse its last row. Keys and values are the label and the content every future asker must still consult. Unlike an RNN, each new query has direct access to all past K and V; nothing is compressed away.

exhibits.title: Flash attention: the same answer in O(n) memory
exhibits.caption: The cost of attention is memory traffic, not only arithmetic. Left, on a log-log scale: eager attention materialises the full (n, n) score matrix in the GPU's large-but-slow HBM, so its memory rises as O(n^2): about 32 GB for a single head at n = 128K. Flash attention never forms that matrix; its footprint is O(n), a near-flat line. Right, how: blocks of Q and K,V are loaded into the tiny, fast on-chip SRAM (~20 MB); for each tile a partial score S = QK^T is computed, folded into a running softmax (a running max m, a running sum l, and the output O, rescaling old partials by e^(m_old - m_new)), then discarded. The (n, n) matrix is never stored anywhere. Crucially the result is IDENTICAL to eager attention, exact, not approximate. If Flash and eager ever disagree, it is a bug, not a feature.
